description: A four-oscillator digital VCO built on vector synthesis: A, B, C and D are drawn at the corners of a diamond and crossfaded by a joystick, by X and Y voltages, or by a timed mix envelope

params.text: Turns to change whichever setting the screen is showing, including the waveform when an oscillator's first page is up
Steps to the next page of the current context, and returns to the first page when held with left Ctrl or left Command
Selects the setting printed beside it on the screen; left Ctrl or left Command with a press returns that setting to its default. On the mix envelope's first page it selects an envelope point
Selects that context and lights the red bar above it. Pressing the one already lit turns all five off, which is the PROGRAM context
Switches the mix envelope on and off for the current program

inputs.text: The pitch of all four oscillators, at 1V per octave; the width of the cable patched here sets the polyphony
Selects the program by voltage, one step every +0.5V from +1V to +8.5V; anything below +1V is ignored and anything above +8.5V gives program 16
Moves the crossfade point sideways in the diamond, adding to the joystick position
Moves the crossfade point up and down in the diamond, adding to the joystick position
The modulating signal for the oscillators, used as linear through-zero FM or as phase modulation, whichever the program's FM page names; the depth is set there too
Starts the mix envelope on a gate of +1V or more and releases it when the gate falls back, and can retrigger the two LFOs

outputs.text: That oscillator on its own, before the crossfade unless its OSC VOLUME page has been set to post-joystick
The four oscillators crossfaded, which is the main output of vector synthesis

notes: the joystick is one widget rather than a control, so it cannot be clicked for help. Dragging it crossfades the four oscillators, and it sets the position of a mix envelope point being edited
the module works in six contexts: A, B, C and D for the oscillators, MIX for the mix envelope, and PROGRAM when none of those five buttons is lit
a program holds the four oscillators, the joystick position, the whole mix envelope, the FM depth and mode and both LFOs. Fifteen of the sixteen are Prophet VS programs, the sixteenth an INIT
waveform 126 is SILENCE and switches that oscillator off; waveform 127 is WHITE NOISE, which has a fixed frequency and cannot be pitched or frequency-modulated.
a WAVE file imported into a user slot must be 2048 samples, 16-bit signed PCM, mono, 44100Hz, and exactly 4140 bytes; anything else is refused.
each imported user waveform is written into the patch as 8192 bytes of text. From the ninth the WARN./ERR. lamp blinks orange to warn that the patch file is growing; clear unused slots
the WARN./ERR. lamp blinks red twice a second when a file operation fails, and the reason appears on the display until any button is pressed.
a right-side VX expander brings the two LFOs, the joystick position and the mix envelope out as voltages.
Randomize does nothing on this module.
the module is polyphonic to sixteen voices, and each of its six contexts has its own pages, stepped through with the PAGE button
menu: Import .wav file as USER # — under User waveform, reads a WAVE file into the user slot the DATA ENTRY encoder is showing; a .wav file dropped on the panel does the same
Clear (free) USER # — under User waveform, empties the user slot now showing, and is greyed when that slot is already empty
Open from .vktMixEnv file — under MIX ENVelope, loads points, rates and loop into the current program; the envelope's on or off state is not part of the file
Save to .vktMixEnv file — under MIX ENVelope, writes the current points, rates and loop to a file
Reset to factory MIX ENVelope — under MIX ENVelope, puts the current program's envelope back to how the program shipped
Open from .vktProgram file — under Program #, loads a saved program into the current program number; the program takes its name from the filename
Save to .vktProgram file — under Program #, writes the current program to a file
Reset to factory program — under Program #, puts the current program back to the Prophet VS setting it shipped with
INITialize this program — under Program #, replaces the current program with the INIT settings

inputs.1:
+1 to +8.5V · stepped · one channel only

a negative voltage does nothing here.
